title: Prime residue and modular batch regions
objective: Implement a guarded complete-batch optimizer plugin for small prime residues and modular arithmetic with indexed inputs/outputs only when aliasing and exact intermediate bounds are proved; compare monomorphic V8, resident Wasm, and coarse native targets including copy/materialization costs; add independent verifier, emitter, tests, and benchmark, leaving central registration to integration.

handoff.summary: Implemented the opt-in math.modular-batch-region.v1 plugin for complete indexed residue batches. The recognizer admits only a top-level builtin range(count) loop immediately preceded by a fresh [None for _slot in range(count)] output allocation, one out[index] assignment, one to four immutable same-index inputs, and a bounded +, -, *, unary -, and exact-integer graph. The representation authenticates parent, element brand/prototype, every used method, and the complete integer-coercion plan; validates and packs the entire input transaction before computation; proves Number exactness through modulus 94,906,266; computes into private Float64 storage; and publishes only after success, with the untouched source loop as guard fallback. An independent verifier re-derives bindings, expression facts, alias proof, method mask, bounds, four-target inclusive structural costs, and code budget. The planner compares V8, resident Wasm, coarse native, and generic execution including copies, conversions, materialization, allocation, boundaries, and cold events; v1 selects only the implemented isolated V8 lowering and records stable capability rejects for Wasm/native. Generated and adversarial tests cover exact BigInt differentials through the maximum modulus and endpoint products, zero trips, alias/access rejects, explicit-contract selection, malformed plans, CPython emitter parsing, and an O0 Sage.js oracle. The 100,000-element benchmark measured 34.49 ms inclusive V8 versus a 1,904.74 ms projected real Sage.js O0 baseline (55.22x), with exact checksum 809625678 and 509 emitted bytes inside a 1,792-byte plan budget. Current successful receipts cover the full build, compiler suite, architecture checks, all seven focused tests, and the benchmark.
risks: Executable registration is intentionally absent from this lane because catalog, lowering registry, verifier catalog, dispatcher, and shared architecture test are integration-owned; until those edits land, the plugin can be inspected and tested directly but cannot be selected by the production compiler.
Resident Wasm and coarse native estimates are inclusive but deliberately rejected until source-derived isolated modular-batch lowerings are registered; v1 does not relabel an unrelated kernel.

The current full integration receipt passed batches 1 and 2, then failed an unrelated dense-prime GF(2) scalar-write host timing ratchet in batch 3 (about 52 microseconds); 282 later files were not started. The current test:changed receipt passed build, architecture checks, and unit batches 1 through 5, then failed an unrelated Chromium group-pack test whose browser server returned HTTP 404 for a runtime asset.
Runtime receipts are Linux x64 only; required Linux arm64, Windows x64, and macOS arm64 validation remains integration/CI work.
